1. Overview & Motivation

In cinematic mathematical and scientific animations, spoken narration serves as the primary cognitive anchor, directing viewer attention across complex derivations, geometric transformations, and algorithmic steps. However, video viewers often watch with muted audio, non-native language comprehension, or accessibility needs. Closed captions and subtitles bridge this gap by transforming audio waveforms into real-time, synchronized visual typography.

In traditional video production, subtitles are either hard-burned via external post-processing tools (FFmpeg, Premiere) or rendered through basic HTML overlays that cannot be integrated into WebGPU render passes or headless video exports.
Retiam introduces a first-class, WebGPU-native subtitle component: [`Subtitles`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/components/Subtitles.ts), available through `retiam/tts`:

items: **Hardware-Accelerated SDF Typography**: Renders multi-line text using signed distance field (MSDF) fonts for crisp typography at any camera zoom level or resolution (1080p, 4K, 8K).

**Mathematically Undistorted Corner Fillets**: Replaces squashed affine scaling with direct vector geometry tessellation (`Builder.roundedRect`), ensuring circular corner arcs regardless of aspect ratio.
**Content-Aware Geometry Reflow**: Automatically calculates text dimensions using local AABB bounding box measurement and adjusts pill padding, line wraps, and corner fillets.

**Integrated Audio Synchronization**: Connects with Retiam's TTS suite ([`TTSClient`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/core/TTSClient.ts), [`Speak`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/animations/Speak.ts), and [`speak()`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/animations/Speak.ts#L186)) for automatic timing, ducking, and auto-clearing.
**Curated Presets & Polymorphic Styling**: Supports seven built-in aesthetic themes (Obsidian, Stadium Pill, Minimal, Broadcast, Neon, Glass, Light) and runtime chainable styling methods.

blocks.text: 3. Geometric Design: Eliminating Corner Radius Distortion
The Affine Scale Trap

In 2D vector graphics engines, a common anti-pattern is creating a normalized or unit rectangle (e.g. $2.0 \times 1.0$) with rounded corners ($r = 0.15$), and then scaling the entity via its transformation matrix to match text width:
Because subtitle banners are wide and relatively short (e.g. $w = 14.0$, $h = 1.6$), the horizontal scale factor $s_x = 7.0$ vastly exceeds the vertical scale factor $s_y = 1.6$.

When this non-uniform transformation matrix multiplies the circular corner arcs, it stretches their axes by $7.0\times$ horizontally and only $1.6\times$ vertically. The resulting corners are transformed into **distorted, squashed ellipses** with an aspect ratio of over $4.3 : 1$.
The Direct Geometry Mutation Pattern
Retiam solves this problem by eliminating non-uniform scaling on the entity transform. The transform scale remains strictly locked at $[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]$.

When subtitle text changes, [`Subtitles`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/components/Subtitles.ts) mutates the geometric properties directly on [`Rect`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Rect.ts):

Inside [`Rect.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Rect.ts#L58-L79), property setters trigger `this.sync()`, which calls [`Builder.roundedRect(-w/2, -h/2, w, h, r)`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/utils/Builder.ts#L132). This tessellates SVG circular arc commands (`A rx ry 0 0 1 x y` where $r_x = r_y = r$), producing circular fillets on all four corners.
Mathematical Corner Clamping

To prevent geometric self-intersection when a large corner radius is applied to a compact box, [`Subtitles`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/components/Subtitles.ts) calculates a safe radius:
If `pillShape: true` is configured, $r_{\text{effective}} = r_{\text{max}} = \frac{h}{2}$, transforming the box into a stadium capsule with semicircular ends.

Long narrations exceed camera viewports if rendered on a single line. When text exceeds `maxLineChars` (default `65`), [`Subtitles`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/components/Subtitles.ts) executes word-wrapping that preserves word boundaries:
2. Dual Bounding-Box Sizing Pipeline
To ensure padding around multi-line text, [`Subtitles`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/components/Subtitles.ts) uses a two-tier measurement pipeline:

items: **Hardware Geometry Measurement**: Calls `this._textEntity.getGroupLocalAABB()` to query actual glyph metrics from `TextGeometry`.
**Heuristic Fallback**: If the geometry is unmeasured or empty (initial frame), it uses font size heuristics:

blocks.text: Total backdrop dimensions are computed with padding margins:
3. Center Origin Alignment

The text entity is configured with `anchor: CENTER`, shifting its local offset to the geometric center of its bounding box. Because [`Rect`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Rect.ts) is centered at $(-w/2, -h/2, w, h)$, both the text and the backdrop share an origin of $(0, 0, 0)$ within the `Subtitles` group.

blocks.text: 8. Best Practices, Pitfalls & Anti-Patterns
1. Never Apply Affine Transform Scaling to Rounded Boxes

Do not call `subtitles.backdrop.transform.setScale([sx, sy, sz])`. Non-uniform scaling squashes corner fillets into ellipses. Always modify `subtitles.setCornerRadius(...)` or `subtitles.applyOptions(...)`, which trigger geometric re-tessellation via `Rect.sync()`.
2. Clamping and Padding Ratios

Keep horizontal padding (`padding[0]`) larger than the corner radius (`cornerRadius`). If horizontal padding is smaller than the corner fillet radius, multi-line text will visually touch the curved corners of the pill.

items: Recommended: `padding[0] >= cornerRadius * 2.0`.

blocks.text: 3. Safe Character Sets for SDF Typography

Retiam's default MSDF atlas (`Font.default`) includes standard ASCII typography (`A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, standard punctuation). Unicode mathematical subscripts (`₁`, `₂`) and operators (`≥`) outside the atlas character map will render as blank spaces.

items: Use standard ASCII notation for narration subtitles (e.g. `x1 + x2 + x3 = 7 (all x >= 0)`).
For mathematical formulas, use Retiam's LaTeX component (`Tex`) rather than raw SDF text strings.

blocks.text: 4. Z-Index Layering

By default, `Subtitles` assigns `zIndex: 999` to the backdrop and `zIndex: 1000` to the SDF text. This keeps subtitles visible above 3D meshes, particle clouds, and 2D geometry while allowing custom UI overlays (such as scene headers or debug inspectors) to render on top by setting `zIndex: 2000`.
9. Verification & Testing
To verify subtitle rendering and check for regression issues without re-rendering videos:

npx retiam lint src/scenes/StarsAndBarsScene.ts --json

# 2. Run TypeScript compilation to check type compatibility
npx tsc --noEmit

# 3. Capture an instant single-frame keyframe snapshot at the subtitle timestamp
npx retiam snapshot src/scenes/StarsAndBarsScene.ts --times 6.0 --out ./outputs/snapshots
